i'd like to run a shiny-app on the server of my institute, which allows people to upload data, get the data processed, and download the data with some additional columns. The app works fine, but i am a little concerned because people will probably upload private data, which they shouldnt. :P I think about checking the uploaded file whether more than the expected data is in it, but i'd still have some question regarding how shiny handles the uploaded data:

1. i guess, everytime someone opens the app he gets kind of a private session, and no one (except server admin) could access or see his data? When two people access the app, do they get independent sessions?
2. when is the uploaded data finally saved (i just store it in the input-object)?

Thanks a lot, Felix

For #1, you can see the article on Scoping: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html. The idea is that you have control over what data is shared and what is stored per session. But the general use case is to keep data private to its own session.

Jeff
